name: LA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+25 partisan lean makes a Democratic loss nearly impossible
Incumbent Troy Carter holds a massive fundraising edge over underfunded opposition
Prediction markets price Carter's win probability at 98 percent
No public polling, but token Republican and third-party spending gives no sign of a contest
model.rationale: Carter represents a New Orleans-based district that leans Democratic by 25 points, and his $1.9 million raised dwarfs the negligible war chests of his rivals. Markets price this at 98 percent Democratic, and with no polls or expert ratings suggesting trouble, the seat sits well outside competitive range.
model.watch: A late-breaking scandal or unexpected surge in opposition outside spending would be the only realistic path to narrowing the margin, though even that is unlikely to threaten the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Troy Carter, a Democratic incumbent seeking another term in this New Orleans-centered district, enters the general election as an overwhelming favorite. The seat's partisan lean of 25 points Democratic, combined with his incumbency and a fundraising total of roughly $1.9 million, leaves Republican Peter Williams with little visible path. Williams has no reported fundraising, and Libertarian and independent candidates in the field have raised only token amounts.

Prediction markets give Carter about a 98 percent chance of winning, and with no public polling or outside spending to suggest otherwise, the race lacks any competitive signal. The expected margin falls in the low-30-point range with moderate uncertainty given the absence of survey data, but the outcome is not seriously in doubt.
